# Assessment — #488: Guardian LAN/mDNS self-advertisement

_Codebase assessment against 0.13.0-beta.3 (2026-07-12). Effort: **M**._

## Current state (already merged)

Acceptance item 1 (no boot-time apk add) is structurally met: the avahi sidecars (mdns-guardian/mdns-assistant) are gone entirely (comment block at /home/user/openpalm/packages/skeleton/system/stack/core.compose.yml:169-176; CHANGELOG.md:213-219; no 'apk add'/'avahi' anywhere under /home/user/openpalm/containers), and /home/user/openpalm/packages/lib/src/control-plane/network-partitioning.test.ts:158-223 asserts their removal. The assistant now relies on OpenCode's NATIVE in-process responder, shipped OFF: /home/user/openpalm/packages/skeleton/system/assistant/opencode.jsonc:49-54 sets "mdns": false with a STATIC "mdnsDomain": "openpalm.local" (not derived from any assistant name — no structured assistant-name exists; persona is free-text markdown at /api/assistant/persona, and OP_PROJECT_NAME is the closest slug). The guardian moderator OpenCode is loopback-bound with mdns:false (/home/user/openpalm/packages/skeleton/system/guardian/opencode.jsonc:16-20). CRITICALLY, the guardian's Bun front door (packages/guardian) has ZERO mDNS code — the issue's 'tiny Bun responder' was never built — and docs/technical/network-partitioning-d5a.md:90-96 records this as an explicit gap ("<name>-guardian.local ... must be advertised by the host OS ... not by an OpenCode process"). Acceptance item 2 (advertise only when LAN enabled) is not wired: nothing couples server.mdns to OP_BIND_ADDRESS/OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS; the admin LAN toggle (/home/user/openpalm/packages/ui/src/routes/api/host/stack/+server.ts:76-93, surfaced as lanExposureEnabled) only writes OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS. Loopback default emits nothing only trivially, because mDNS is statically off. Acceptance item 3 (admin UI surfaces the .local name) is not implemented — grep for mdns in packages/ui returns nothing; the LAN Exposure card (/home/user/openpalm/packages/ui/src/lib/components/admin/assistant/AssistantTab.svelte:136-148) shows no .local name. D5a further documents that native container mDNS never reaches the physical LAN on the default bridge network (needs network_mode: host on Linux; inert on macOS), and that OpenCode's Bonjour instance label is hardcoded 'opencode-4096' — both push the remaining implementation toward a responder in the HOST-side control-plane process (the openpalm CLI/UI server, /home/user/openpalm/packages/cli/src/lib/ui-server.ts + /home/user/openpalm/packages/ui/src/hooks.server.ts), which runs on the real host network.

## Remaining work

- [ ] Ratify the advertisement locus and record it in docs/technical/network-partitioning-d5a.md: implement the 'tiny Bun responder' in the HOST control-plane process (started from packages/cli/src/lib/ui-server.ts or packages/ui/src/hooks.server.ts init, next to the existing collectBindAddressWarnings call at hooks.server.ts:59) rather than inside the guardian container, because D5a shows bridge-network multicast never reaches the LAN and network_mode: host would break the partitioning invariants. The issue text's in-guardian responder should be explicitly rejected or accepted with the host-network tradeoff documented.
- [ ] Implement a minimal mDNS responder module, e.g. packages/lib/src/control-plane/mdns-responder.ts: join 224.0.0.251:5353 via node:dgram, answer A/PTR/SRV/TXT queries for the advertised names; keep DNS packet encode/decode as pure exported functions so they are unit-testable without sockets.
- [ ] Gating logic: advertise '<name>-guardian.local' (targeting the guardian host port, OP_GUARDIAN_PORT default 3830 per packages/skeleton/system/stack/portals.compose.yml:148) only when OP_BIND_ADDRESS is non-loopback; advertise '<name>.local' (assistant host port) only when OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS resolves non-loopback (the lanExposureEnabled semantics in packages/ui/src/routes/api/host/stack/+server.ts:52). Export/reuse isLoopback from packages/lib/src/control-plane/bind-warning.ts:22 instead of duplicating it. Loopback-only default must start no socket at all.
- [ ] Name derivation: derive the base label from OP_PROJECT_NAME in knowledge/env/stack.env (readStackEnv from @openpalm/lib; default 'openpalm'), sanitized to a DNS label — giving openpalm.local / openpalm-guardian.local by default. Decide whether the assistant's native OpenCode mdns/mdnsDomain block in packages/skeleton/system/assistant/opencode.jsonc stays as a documented advanced/manual path (recommended) or gets file-assembled to match the derived name on install/upgrade.
- [ ] Admin UI surface: extend the GET /api/host/stack payload (packages/ui/src/routes/api/host/stack/+server.ts) with the derived .local names and their active/inactive state, and render them in the LAN Exposure card of packages/ui/src/lib/components/admin/assistant/AssistantTab.svelte when enabled (per #557, prefer surfacing the HTTPS/ts.net name once guardian TLS lands — coordinate the displayed scheme).
- [ ] Tests: unit tests for packet encode/decode and gating in packages/lib (new mdns-responder.test.ts following the fixture style of network-partitioning.test.ts); extend network-partitioning.test.ts to keep asserting the guardian moderator stays mdns:false/loopback and the assistant skeleton ships mdns:false; add vitest cases to packages/ui/src/routes/api/host/stack/server.vitest.ts for the new payload fields.
- [ ] Docs: refresh docs/technical/network-partitioning-d5a.md mDNS section and CHANGELOG for the host-side responder; note the macOS/Linux behavior (host process multicast works on both, closing the container-mDNS gap).

## Test strategy

packages/lib runs plain `bun test` (packages/lib/package.json script "test": "bun test"); write the responder test-first as packages/lib/src/control-plane/mdns-responder.test.ts covering pure DNS packet encode/decode (A/PTR/SRV/TXT answers), name derivation/sanitization from OP_PROJECT_NAME, and the gating truth table (OP_BIND_ADDRESS / OP_ASSISTANT_BIND_ADDRESS loopback vs non-loopback → which names advertise, loopback default → responder not started), following the socket-free fixture style of network-partitioning.test.ts (which parses the skeleton compose/jsonc files from REPO_ROOT). Extend network-partitioning.test.ts to keep the invariants: guardian moderator mdns:false + hostname 127.0.0.1, assistant ships mdns:false. packages/ui unit tests run via vitest (`bun run test:unit -- --run`; files match *.vitest.ts): add cases to packages/ui/src/routes/api/host/stack/server.vitest.ts asserting the GET payload includes the derived .local names and their enabled state, and that PUT toggling lanExposureEnabled flips them. If any guardian-package code is touched, packages/guardian runs `bun test --no-orphans`. Manual/e2e verification: on a Linux host with OP_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0, `avahi-resolve -n openpalm-guardian.local` (or `dns-sd -G v4`) from another LAN machine; with the loopback default, confirm no UDP 5353 socket is bound (ss -ulpn).

## Dependencies (0.13.0 open issues)

- #557 (soft, coordination): its scope explicitly says 'Coordinate with #488 — mDNS advertisement should surface the HTTPS name when enabled'; the admin-UI surfacing work should agree with #557 on whether the displayed reachable name is http://<name>-guardian.local:3830 or the TLS (ts.net/Caddy) name once guardian edge TLS lands. Not a hard blocker — the responder, gating, and default http surfacing can land first.

## Risks

- mDNS responder correctness: hand-rolling multicast DNS in Bun (dgram membership, shared 5353 binding alongside host OS responders like avahi-daemon/Bonjour via SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT) is fiddly; conflicts with an existing host responder can cause silent non-answers or EADDRINUSE.
- Architecture divergence from the issue text: the issue asks for the responder in the guardian (container), but the ratified D5a analysis shows container mDNS cannot reach the LAN on bridge networks — the assessment recommends the host control-plane process instead; this decision needs explicit sign-off or the acceptance criteria re-read.
- The host UI/CLI process is not guaranteed to be running whenever the stack is (e.g. stack started, `openpalm` supervisor exited) — advertisement would silently stop; may need to document that or advertise from a longer-lived host component.
- Security posture: must stay fail-closed — any bug that advertises on the loopback-only default violates the 'never public without explicit opt-in' invariant; gating must be tested exhaustively.
- The '<assistant-name>' concept does not exist as structured data; using OP_PROJECT_NAME may surprise users who consider their persona name the assistant name.
- OpenCode native responder's hardcoded 'opencode-4096' instance label remains a cosmetic regression if the assistant-side native path is kept as the advertised mechanism.

## Original issue body

# #488: Guardian LAN/mDNS self-advertisement

Spun out of #436 (Part 2) and #432 (Phase 6). Network partitioning landed in 0.12.0; the **mDNS self-advertisement** piece is deferred to 0.13.0.

## Scope
When LAN access is explicitly enabled (via `OP_BIND_ADDRESS`, #395), the guardian and (optionally) the assistant advertise themselves on the local network over mDNS:
- Guardian advertises as `<assistant-name>-guardian.local`.
- When assistant LAN access is enabled, assistant advertises as `<assistant-name>.local`.

## Notes / current state (0.12.0)
- mDNS is currently **scaffolded but default-off**; the sidecar uses `apk add` at container boot rather than a baked image — replace with a baked image / a tiny Bun responder (the guardian is a Bun process, not an OpenCode process, so OpenCode `--mdns` does not apply).
- Must stay **off by default**; only advertises when LAN exposure is explicitly opted in. Never public without explicit opt-in.

## Acceptance
- [ ] mDNS responder baked (no boot-time `apk add`).
- [ ] Advertises only when LAN access is enabled; loopback-only default emits nothing.
- [ ] Admin UI surfaces the `.local` name when enabled.
